trial_court: I Additional Family Judge, Family Court, Bangalore, M.C.No.3726/2019
case_name: Smt. Pratibha Singh vs Mr. Vineet Kumar
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The petitioner is the wife and respondent is her husband. They got married on 22-04-2016. The wife left the matrimonial house after about six months of marriage and began residing in her parental house. The husband registered a petition seeking annulment of marriage under Section 13(1)(ia) & (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A wife is entitled to maintenance if she is receiving sufficient income.
legal_principles.held: On the other hand, during the pendency of the petition, if the wife is receiving sufficient income, then she is entitled to get the maintenance from the husband.

legal_principles.principle: A person's own statement cannot be believable if not supported by material evidence.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, her own statement could not be believable. Also, the respondent could not deny that he is having income of `3,50,000/-.

legal_principles.principle: A person's income is sufficient to lead a happy life if it equals the status of their spouse.
legal_principles.held: The said salary is totally sufficient to lead the happy life equal to the status of the petitioner?

legal_principles.principle: A person's expenses include conveyance charges and day-to-day expenses.
legal_principles.held: On the other hand, the respondent out of that salary amount she has to meet the conveyance charges and that contention of the respondent could not be ignored.

outcome.final_order: The court granted interim maintenance to the petitioner/wife at `15,000/- and litigation expenses at `50,000/-. The court also enhanced the same to `1,50,000/- per month as interim maintenance and `2,00,000/- as one time litigation expenses.
